overall: The AG found the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by holding the open session portion of its December 12, 2022 meeting in a locked building, but found no violation in the executive session rights claim; ordered future compliance only.

allegations.summary: The December 12 meeting's open session was held in a town hall whose doors had locked automatically, so a member of the public could not get in at the start time.
allegations.key_passage: By holding this open session portion of the meeting in a locked building the Board violated the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: A complainant argued that, as the complainant on the Open Meeting Law complaint being discussed, he could insist the executive session be held in open session or be audio recorded.
allegations.key_passage: We have explained that a public body may discuss a complaint about the public body in executive session if a majority of the public body has voted to do so.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law's requirements (no further remedial action ordered).
Caution that a similar, future violation may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
remedy_passage: We order the Board’s immediate and future compliance with the law’s requirements, and caution the Board that a similar, future violation may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
